implementation_notes: Kotlin turns the collecting parameter into a stdlib builder function: `buildString { ... }` and `buildList { ... }` create the mutable accumulator, pass it as the lambda receiver (producers call `append`/`add` on `this`) and return the final `String`/read-only `List`. The mutable receiver is documented as valid only inside the builder lambda, which is exactly the pattern's scope discipline enforced by convention plus the API. `StringBuilder`/`MutableList` still work as explicit parameters when the accumulator must outlive one lambda, and `fold`/`joinToString` replace the pattern when the producers are elements of a collection.
pitfalls: Letting the builder's receiver escape the lambda is unspecified behaviour - kotlinlang.org states the `MutableList` receiver 'is valid only inside that function'; copy it out with `toList()`.
`buildList` returns a read-only list, so producers cannot append after the lambda ends - streaming or async accumulation needs an explicit `MutableList` parameter instead.
A mutable collection can still be upcast back to `MutableList`: code that hands the builder out as a mutable type lets callers modify a result that was supposed to be frozen.
